bun-shared-memory — LLM Reference

PACKAGE: bun-shared-memory v1.0.0
REPO: Kapsonfire/bun-shared-memory
LICENSE: MIT
RUNTIME: Bun >= 1.4.0 (also works in Node.js and browser Web Workers)

QUICK SUMMARY
=============
A TypeScript library for the Bun runtime that shares data between workers/threads
using SharedArrayBuffer. Zero-copy, high-performance, with a Proxy-based API and
Atomics-based synchronization. Supports objects (fixed shape), arrays, primitives,
bigints, and nested structures.

CORE API
========

1. Shared<T>(key, value, options?) -> SharedRef<T>
   Get or create a typed wrapper for a value in shared memory.

   Examples:
     const user = Shared("user-1", { name: "Alice", age: 30 });
     user.name = "Bob";                    // writes to shared memory
     console.log(user.age);                // reads from shared memory
     const scores = Shared("scores", [1, 2, 3]);
     scores.push(4);                       // O(1) amortized
     scores[0] = 100;                      // direct index write

     // Async loader (runs once, first caller wins)
     const config = await Shared("config", async () => loadConfig());

     // Options
     const mem = new SharedMemory({ maxTotalBytes: 64 * 1024 * 1024 });
     const obj = Shared("obj", { x: 1 }, { memory: mem, arrayCapacity: 16 });

2. SharedRef<T> — Returned Wrapper
   For objects: properties are directly accessible (hard-baked accessors)
   For arrays: Proxy with index access and mutating methods
   For primitives: Proxy

   Methods:
     read(): T                    - Read full value (with deep copy)
     write(value: T): void        - Write full value to shared memory
     update(fn: (current: T) => T): T  - Atomic read-modify-write
     key: string                  - The shared key name (readonly)
     buffer: SharedArrayBuffer    - Underlying SAB (readonly)

3. SharedMemory — Core Memory Manager
   const mem = new SharedMemory({
     initialSize?: number,            // default: 1024
     maxByteLength?: number,          // default: 64 MiB, min 32 MiB
     maxTotalBytes?: number,          // combined budget for Data/Str/Arr tables
     chunkSize?: number,              // default: 32 MiB, min 4 MiB
     lock?: Mutex,                    // global mutex; its buffer also holds the 256 key lock stripes
     internCapacity?: number,         // string interning cache, default: 256
     internMax?: number,              // intern cache max entries, default: 65536
   });

   Methods:
     exportBuffers() -> {...}        // export all SABs for worker handoff
     static fromBuffers(buffers)     // reconstruct from exported buffers
     storeString(value) -> StringRef // intern string (append-only, deduped)
     readString(ref: StringRef)
     storeArray(slots, capacity?) -> ArrayRef
     readArray(ref: ArrayRef)
     appendArraySlot(ref, slot) -> ArrayRef  // O(1) amortized push
     createObject(properties: [name, ValueSlot][]) -> offset
     readObject(offset) -> [name, ValueSlot][]
     getObjectLayout(key) -> ObjectLayout|null
     lookup(key) -> offset|null
     lookupIndex(key) -> index|null
     insert(key, dataOffset)
     getKeyByIndex(index) -> string|null
     bumpVersion(index)              // invalidate read caches cross-worker
     getLayoutVersion() -> number
     bumpLayoutVersion()
     beginWrite(), endWrite()        // lock-free write coordination
     isDefragmenting() -> boolean
     waitForWritesToFinish()
     defragment() -> {...buffers}    // compact, reclaim dead space

4. Mutex — Atomics-Based Re-entrant Lock
   const mutex = new Mutex(buffer?: SharedArrayBuffer);
   mutex.lock()                      // acquire (blocks with Atomics.wait)
   mutex.unlock()                    // release (wakes waiters)
   mutex.withLock(fn)                // run fn under lock
   mutex.buffer                      // underlying SAB

5. Notifier — Atomics-Based Signaling
   const notifier = new Notifier(buffer?: SharedArrayBuffer);
   notifier.wait(timeoutMs?)         // -> "ok" | "not-equal" | "timed-out"
   notifier.notify(count = 1)        // wake up to N waiting workers

6. Worker Integration
   Main thread:
     import { init, spawnWorker, acceptWorker, stopInit } from "bun-shared-memory";
     await init({ maxTotalBytes: 64 * 1024 * 1024 });  // sets up refcount coordinator
     const worker = spawnWorker(new URL("./worker.ts", import.meta.url), { type: "module" });
     // or acceptWorker(worker) for browser environments
     stopInit();                     // cleanup

   Worker:
     import { init, onMessage } from "bun-shared-memory";
     await init();                    // receives shared buffers from main thread
     Shared("myKey", { data: 42 });  // now shares with main thread
     onMessage((e) => { /* handle messages */ });

7. Environment Detection
   import { isBun, isMainThread, isWorkerContext, isNode } from "bun-shared-memory";

MEMORY ARCHITECTURE (4 + 1 BUFFERS)
====================================
1) Index Table    - maps object keys -> DataTable offsets
   Single growable SAB, max 4 GiB, O(n) linear key scan

2) DataTable      - stores objects + value slots
   Chunked, variable-length blocks (OBJECT type, primitive value slots)

3) StringTable    - append-only storage for strings
   Chunked, deduped via per-worker LRU interning cache

4) ArrayTable     - append-only storage for arrays
   Chunked, capacity padding for O(1) push, relocate on overflow (doubled capacity)

5) RefCountBuffer - ring buffer + heartbeat + global refcount table
   Auto-started by init() for auto-GC

Value Slot Layout (16 bytes each):
  [0..3]   type (Int32):
           0=number, 1=boolean, 2=bigint, 3=string-ref, 4=array-ref,
           5=object, 6=bigint-str, 7=string-value-ref, 8=inline-string,
           9=object-ref, 10=key-ref, 11=null
  [4..7]   payload A (offset / int32)
  [8..11]  payload B (length / count / int32)
  [12..15] payload C (capacity / int32)

Object Block Layout in DataTable:
  [0..3]   type = 5 (OBJECT)
  [4..7]   property count
  [8..11]  objectId (monotonic, stable across defragmentation)
  [12..15] reserved
  then for each property:
    [name_offset(4) + name_length(4)] -> into StringTable
    [value_type(4) + payload_A(4) + payload_B(4) + payload_C(4)]

Index Table Entry (16 bytes):
  [0..3]   key string offset (into StringTable)
  [4..7]   key string length
  [8..11]  data offset (into DataTable)
  [12..15] key version (Int32, bumped on every write)

SUPPORTED TYPES
===============
  JS Type     | Storage                  | Notes
  ------------|--------------------------|------------------------------------------
  number      | Inline in slot (float64) |
  boolean     | Inline in slot           |
  bigint      | Inline if fits int64     | Large bigints stored as StringTable
  string      | StringTable or inline    | Inline for <=11 bytes; deduped via interning
  null        | TYPE_NULL slot           | undefined is NOT supported
  Array       | ArrayTable (append-only) | Mixed types allowed; nested arrays supported
  object      | DataTable block          | FIXED SHAPE: properties may NOT be added/removed
  Shared obj  | Live key reference       | Stays in sync with referenced key

SYNCHRONIZATION MODEL
=====================
1. Per-key write locks: a write holds the lock stripe of its key (256 re-entrant
   Mutex stripes, keyIndex & 255). Writers to different keys run in parallel,
   writers to the same key are serialized. Key creation and defragmentation use
   the global Mutex (defragmentation takes every stripe + the global Mutex).
2. Read Cache: Each worker caches decoded values with a version number. Writes bump
   the version cell (in the Index Table), so caches auto-invalidate cross-worker.
   Reads of unchanged values are lock-free (plain read of the version cell, they
   scale across workers); object-property reads are lock-free and validated
   (a seqlock: writers mark the version cell, a read that overlapped a write
   decodes again); a whole-value read after a change takes the key's stripe.
3. Offset Cache: Per-worker cache of key -> DataTable offsets, invalidated on
   defragmentation (via layoutVersion).
4. Layout Version: Global cell bumped on GC/defragmentation, invalidating offset
   and layout caches across all workers.
5. Bounded waits: every lock wait times out (default 30 s, LockTimeoutError);
   a dead worker's locks are released by the RefCountCoordinator.
6. One SharedMemory per thread, created on the main thread only; workers get it
   through init() / SharedMemory.fromBuffers().
7. Atomic Registration: Initial value writes hold the lock, so racing workers from
   different threads don't overwrite each other's values.

PERFORMANCE OPTIMIZATIONS
=========================
- String interning: Repeated strings share the same StringTable ref (per-worker LRU cache)
- Inline short strings: <=11 UTF-8 bytes stored directly in the slot (no heap alloc)
- In-place updates: Numbers/booleans/biggints written directly without ValueSlot allocation
- String value reuse: Overwriting with a shorter string reuses existing ArrayTable block
- Array capacity padding: push writes into reserved slots (O(1) amortized); reallocates on overflow
- Hard-baked accessors: Objects get plain JS objects with getters/setters (no Proxy overhead)
- Field cache: Each property getter has its own cache (avoids Map lookup per read)
- Target cache: __cache, __offset, __arrayRef on proxy targets skip Map lookups on writes
- Defragmentation: Auto-runs when free space < 20%, compacts all tables in-place
- Background maintenance: Timer drains refcount events and runs defrag every 100ms (unref'd)

MEMORY BUDGET
=============
- Index Table: Max 4 GiB (single growable SAB), excluded from maxTotalBytes
- DataTable/StringTable/ArrayTable: Chunked buffers, each max maxByteLength (default 64 MiB, min 32 MiB)
- maxTotalBytes: Caps combined physical size of the three chunked tables. Atomic counter shared
  across workers; throws RangeError on overflow.
- chunkSize: Minimum growth step (default 32 MiB, min 4 MiB). Raised as needed so no table
  exceeds 1024 chunks.

REFERENCE COUNTING (AUTO-GC)
=============================
When init() is called on the main thread, a RefCountCoordinator starts automatically:
- Workers have RefCountTracker instances with FinalizationRegistry
- Ring buffer message queue: workers send acquire/release events to main thread
- Heartbeat table: main thread detects dead workers via heartbeat stalls (3 ticks)
- Defragmentation reclaims dead space when free space is low (80% threshold)
- Crash recovery: main thread releases all refs on worker close event (Bun) or
  heartbeat stall (browser)

FILE STRUCTURE
==============
  src/
    index.ts           - Public exports
    memory.ts          - Core 4-buffer SharedMemory (1661 lines)
    shared.ts          - Proxy-based Shared/SharedRef API (2105 lines)
    growable-buffer.ts - Growable SAB helper + SharedBudget (chunked)
    mutex.ts           - Re-entrant Atomics mutex
    notifier.ts        - Atomics wait/notify signaling
    refcount.ts        - RefCountBuffer, RefCountCoordinator, RefCountTracker
    worker.ts          - Worker handshake: init(), spawnWorker(), acceptWorker()
    env.ts             - Environment detection (isBun, isMainThread, etc.)
  dist/esm/            - Compiled ESM output
  test/                - Test files
  bench/               - Benchmarks
  examples/            - Example projects (todo-list, worker)
